summary.name: Vintage Rubber Hose Animation. An authored Motion Graphic in Animation Techniques: early sound-era hand-inked cel cartoon drawing with stepped, elastic acting; its only optional effects are film wear and a vintage film-leader countdown.
summary.visualIdentity: Self-contained identity: strong irregular ink silhouettes, organic contours with varied line weight, interlocking asymmetrical drawn masses, articulated structural details, overlaps and coherent perspective. Colour the hand-inked forms with flat cel fills and bold painterly or cel shadow masses, preserving structural detail. Scenery uses foreground, midground and background planes, atmospheric separation, directional light, contact shadows and selective edge highlights. Environmental acting is mandatory wherever scenery is present: architecture rocks, structural parts flex or skew, trees sway and branches move independently; other settings use equivalent acting with readable holds. Characters, when present, may be any original subject with rounded elastic masses and jointless hose limbs; shots without characters are valid.
summary.decisionGuidance: Identity: early hand-inked cel cartoon drawing with irregular ink silhouettes, painterly shadow masses, expressive scenery and stepped elastic acting. Advantages: warm, playful, hand-made character and environment performance for any original subject, with optional film wear and a precise vintage leader for period flavour. Disadvantages: needs authored key drawings and consistent construction; it reads as nostalgic rather than sleek. Combination fit: stands alone; Traditional Cel Animation can supply drawn frames and data storytelling can add inked diagrams. Visual constraints: original subjects only, flat fills and ink contours, self-contained drawing and tonal requirements with colour overrides scoped to explicitly requested scenes, no neon, glossy 3D or clean corporate vector icons unless requested.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: stories, intros, explainers and title moments that want an early hand-drawn cartoon feel, with or without characters. Inferred: brand, education and entertainment pieces built around an original subject. Not suited to photoreal, glossy 3D or clean corporate vector briefs. Audience is unspecified.
summary.limitations: Never imitate an existing cartoon character, mascot, recognizable silhouette or reference composition. No subject, story, setting or sequence is required. Avoid neon, glossy gradients and heavy saturation unless requested. Keep flashes to three per second or fewer; an optional film leader is a creative hybrid, not a strict historical reconstruction.
summary.palette: Default tonal structure: charcoal ink silhouettes, muted grey/brown midtones, aged ivory lights and deep shadow masses. Recolour only when explicitly requested for this style's assigned scenes, retaining tonal contrast; palettes assigned to other scenes must not bleed in. Optional example tokens: ink black #25221F, aged ivory #F1E3C6, sepia brown #856548, dusty grey #77736D, muted rust #B5523A, vintage gold #E8B65B, faded teal #7EA9A3 and pale sky blue #B9D8D2. These example tokens do not require a sepia tint.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: stepped drawings, typically 12 per second against a 24 fps film reference, from absolute time; expressive elastic poses with anticipation, squash and stretch, overshoot, arcs and rhythmic timing; readable holds without a mandatory perpetual bounce. Environmental acting is required wherever scenery is present; moving texture alone is insufficient. Optional effects only: film wear on the whole plate, and a leader with precise rings and crosshairs, a pale bold sans-serif numeral and a rotating clock-wipe sector.
summary.audio: Optional ideas governed by the project's audio settings: jazz percussion, upright bass, muted brass, playful woodwinds, cartoon sound effects, projector noise or vinyl hiss with film wear, and clicks with an optional leader. Do not invent narration or music when audio is disabled. Audio remains governed by project settings.
summary.assetRequirements: Subjects, any characters, story, copy, duration, aspect ratio, resolution and frame rate come from the project; drawing style, atmosphere, tonal structure and motion follow the written metadata. Everything can be code-drawn with system fonts; supplied hand-drawn cels can replace coded drawings. The drawing rate is animation sampling, not the delivery frame rate.
summary.combinations: Usually used alone. Traditional Cel Animation (style-081) can supply drawn cel frames; Scientific Visualization / Data Storytelling (style-097) can add explanatory diagrams in the same ink and palette.
summary.productionApproach: Use the written drawing and motion requirements as the complete visual contract. Review rendered frames at delivery size for articulated silhouettes, structural detail, depth planes, shadow grouping and highlights; inspect the artwork with optional surface effects disabled. Review stepped key poses, readable holds and independent environmental acting over time. SVG and HTML/CSS draw ink, cels, scenery, any characters and text; Canvas 2D or SVG filters and Rough.js are added only for optional film wear or line boil. The optional leader is precise geometry kept separate from the cartoon artwork. GSAP drives one paused timeline through pure time-state functions. Composition and export follow the project renderer.
